entities.summary: Charles the Child, King of Aquitaine from October 855 until his death in 866, played a crucial role in the medieval era. As the ruler of Aquitaine, he worked closely with Charlemagne, the Holy Roman Emperor, to strengthen the region's ties with the Frankish Empire. This collaboration had significant effects on the development of Western Europe, including the spread of Christianity and the establishment of the Carolingian Renaissance. The legacy of Charles the Child can be seen in the continued influence of the Carolingian Empire on French and European history. He left behind a lasting cultural footprint in the form of the Carolingian Code, a comprehensive set of laws that shaped the administrative and legal systems of medieval Europe. The Carolingian Code remains an important historical artifact, providing valuable insights into the social, political, and economic structures of the time. In the years following his death, the Duchy of Aquitaine continued to play a significant role in European politics, with Charles the Child's descendants going on to shape the region's history for centuries to come.
